Close to the Hebrew; NKJV supplies “He” as subject, “He turned into fear for me.”
NKJV renders צָפֹה (“spread out” or “watch”) as “Set a watchman in the tower,” and the participles as imperatives.
NKJV renders “rider” as “chariot” and “a pair of horses” as “a pair of horsemen.”
NKJV keeps the MT “A lion” (some read “the seer”), and “O Lord” is rendered “my Lord.”
